channel.title: Andrew's Agent Picks
channel.description: A bounded, agent-curated reading feed for Andrew's Matter Inbox.

item.title: 4 engineering patterns behind the strongest AI Agents Challenge submissions
item.dc:creator: Sergio Villani
item.description: Summary: Google identifies four recurring patterns in top agent systems: bidirectional MCP interfaces, event-driven concurrency, shared validation across model fallbacks, and tiered routing before expensive inference. Why it matters for Andrew: These are directly usable design checks for Andrew's personal-agent stack, especially keeping context bounded behind tools, parallelizing independent work, and enforcing the same quality bar when models or paths change. Lane: Ai-agents. Agent relevance score: 94/100.

item.title: Automated researchers can reliably mitigate alignment failures
item.dc:creator: Anthropic
item.description: Summary: Claude autonomously searched the literature, proposed training methods, ran experiments, and improved ten categories of alignment failure, with successful methods transferring to withheld benchmarks and models up to 4.7 times larger. Why it matters for Andrew: This is a concrete blueprint for Andrew's agent buildout: iterative research loops can produce durable improvements when they have mechanical evaluations, capability guardrails, and a separate monitoring agent to catch gaming. Lane: Ai-agents. Agent relevance score: 93/100.

item.title: Enabling independent research on how people use Claude
item.dc:creator: Anthropic Research
item.description: Summary: Anthropic reports a privacy-preserving pilot in which independent researchers analyzed roughly 250,000 Claude and Claude Code conversations, finding frequent delegation of consequential work, continued human direction, and productive collaboration friction. Why it matters for Andrew: The real-world evidence gives Andrew concrete design signals for personal-agent oversight: keep humans directing consequential work, preserve useful friction, and treat approval boundaries as part of the workflow rather than an obstacle. Lane: Ai-agents. Agent relevance score: 93/100.

item.title: Automating repetitive work at OpenAI with Codex
item.dc:creator: Jeremy Lewi
item.description: Summary: Jeremy Lewi explains how Codex, Runme notebooks, and WebMCP turn recurring engineering work into reviewed workflows that capture goals, commands, outputs, decisions, and lessons for reuse. Why it matters for Andrew: This is almost a blueprint for Andrew's agent operating system: keep durable context beside execution, retain human approval at consequential choices, and make every run improve the next one. Lane: Ai-agents. Agent relevance score: 97/100.

item.title: Scaling cyber defenders with Daybreak
item.dc:creator: Mike Aiello
item.description: Summary: OpenAI lays out evidence-first security workflows across ChatGPT, Codex Security review, repository scans, and continuous checks, with scoped access, threat models, isolated validation, and human-reviewed fixes. Why it matters for Andrew: As Andrew expands agents, plugins, and automations, this offers a durable pattern for moving from suspected issues to verified evidence and reviewed remediation without giving agents unchecked authority. Lane: Ai-agents. Agent relevance score: 92/100.

item.title: Piloting the world's first double-blind AI evaluations
item.dc:creator: William Isaac, Sol Messing, and Kristian Lum
item.description: Summary: Google DeepMind describes a double-blind evaluation architecture that uses confidential computing to keep proprietary model weights hidden from evaluators while keeping confidential test prompts hidden from the model provider. Why it matters for Andrew: Andrew relies on model and agent evaluations to guide tooling choices; this is a strong design pattern for reducing benchmark contamination and making external eval results more trustworthy. Lane: Ai-agents. Agent relevance score: 94/100.

item.title: How to Evaluate Live & Voice Agents in ADK
item.dc:creator: Stephen Allen
item.description: Summary: Google shows how to test multi-turn voice-agent workflows with simulated audio users, fixed or dynamic scenarios, natural-language trajectory rubrics, tool-call scoring, replayable transcripts, and CI integration. Why it matters for Andrew: This gives Andrew a concrete evaluation loop for future voice and multi-agent workflows: simulate realistic users, score full trajectories and tool use, cap runaway turns, and catch regressions before deployment. Lane: Ai-agents. Agent relevance score: 95/100.

item.title: How Claude is accelerating protein design and analytical chemistry
item.dc:creator: Anthropic Research
item.description: Summary: Anthropic reports wet-lab validation of Claude-designed protein binders against 14 of 15 targets, plus autonomous NMR and LC-MS analysis that matched a contract lab's results in minutes rather than days. Why it matters for Andrew: This is a durable end-to-end scientific-agent pattern: autonomous orchestration of specialist models, connectors, compute, raw instrument files, and iterative self-checks, with external validation still required. It is useful for Andrew's decisions about where personal agents can act independently and where verification must remain explicit. Lane: Ai-agents. Agent relevance score: 91/100.

item.title: Build zero-trust AI agents with Google's Agent Development Kit
item.dc:creator: Shubham Saboo and Eric Dong
item.description: Summary: Google presents an open-source ADK reference agent secured with per-agent signed writes, gVisor no-egress code isolation, deterministic input and output gateways, and CI regression tests for security policies. Why it matters for Andrew: This turns prompt-injection concerns into enforceable controls for agents that mutate state: signed writes, sandboxed execution, semantic validation, and regression tests. It gives Andrew a concrete checklist for hardening local automations and Matter-adjacent workflows as agent permissions expand. Lane: Ai-agents. Agent relevance score: 95/100.

item.title: Agent and Model Evaluations in Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform are now GA
item.dc:creator: Alex Martin and Dima Melnyk
item.description: Summary: Google describes a unified agent-evaluation system spanning offline experiments and production traces, with versioned metrics, adaptive rubrics, tool-trajectory scoring, failure clustering, simulated users and environments, continuous monitoring, and drift alerts. Why it matters for Andrew: This is a strong blueprint for Andrew's agent-quality loop: keep development and live measurements comparable, grade observable outcomes and tool use, simulate hard cases, cluster failures, and turn production traces into targeted improvements rather than relying on anecdotal success. Lane: Ai-agents. Agent relevance score: 95/100.

item.title: Enable on-demand expertise with Agent Skills in Genkit Go
item.dc:creator: Daniela Petruzalek
item.description: Summary: Google gives a concrete Genkit Go implementation of Agent Skills using SKILL.md bundles, metadata-first discovery, dynamic activation, progressive loading of instructions and resources, and middleware hooks around model and tool execution. Why it matters for Andrew: The article directly mirrors Andrew's modular skill architecture and adds an independent implementation reference for progressive disclosure, trigger descriptions, resource bundling, and runtime activation—useful for tightening skill design and evaluating portability across agent frameworks. Lane: Ai-agents. Agent relevance score: 92/100.

item.title: How we built a realtime system for responsive voice AI in six months
item.dc:creator: Justin Uberti and Zahan Malkani
item.description: Summary: OpenAI explains GPT-Live's full-duplex streaming architecture, asynchronous delegation to frontier models, dynamic context compaction, low-latency transport, and shadow production testing for long-running voice sessions. Why it matters for Andrew: The separation of a fast conversational path from slower reasoning and tool work is a durable design pattern for Andrew's personal-agent interface, while the compaction, session-affinity, and shadow-testing lessons sharpen how to build responsive agents without sacrificing depth or reliability. Lane: Ai-agents. Agent relevance score: 94/100.

item.title: Patterns and problems in emerging multiagent systems
item.dc:creator: Anthropic Frontier Red Team
item.description: Summary: Anthropic studies coordinated agent swarms across vulnerability discovery, shared-code work, hidden-profile decisions, and conflicting objectives, showing both improving coordination and systemic failure modes caused by conformity, weak information sharing, and incompatible goals. Why it matters for Andrew: This is unusually actionable for Andrew's growing use of agent teams: it shows where parallelization helps, why identical agents can create correlated errors, and why dissent, ownership boundaries, and arbitration need to be designed into multi-agent workflows. Lane: Ai-agents. Agent relevance score: 96/100.

item.title: Claude plays robotics
item.dc:creator: Anthropic Research
item.description: Summary: Anthropic tested language models across simulated and physical robot bodies using control interfaces ranging from direct motor commands to high-level steering, measuring where language-model reasoning transfers to embodied tasks. Why it matters for Andrew: This is a concrete test of how agent capability changes with tool abstraction and environment design—useful for Andrew’s work on agent interfaces, verification, and deciding what should remain under human control. Lane: Ai-agents. Agent relevance score: 90/100.

item.title: Building self-improving tax agents with Codex
item.dc:creator: Aravind Srinivasan, Samay Shamdasani, Arthur Fernandes Araujo, and John de Wasseige
item.description: Summary: OpenAI and Thrive describe a three-part loop that turns practitioner corrections and production traces into reviewed findings, targeted evals, bounded Codex tasks, and regression-tested improvements for a tax-preparation agent. Why it matters for Andrew: The evidence-to-eval-to-agent loop maps directly onto Andrew’s personal-agent improvement workflow, while the rental-property example makes it unusually relevant to both his knowledge-base system and duplex operations. Lane: Ai-agents. Agent relevance score: 95/100.

item.title: Building scalable AI agents with modular prompt transpilation
item.dc:creator: Simerus Mahesh
item.description: Summary: Google proposes treating prompts as compiled software artifacts: modular skill files are transpiled with dependency checks, static validation, drift detection, CI enforcement, and progressive runtime loading. Why it matters for Andrew: This directly stress-tests Andrew’s modular SKILL.md and AGENTS.md architecture and offers concrete build-time controls for preventing instruction drift as the personal agent system compounds. Lane: Ai-agents. Agent relevance score: 93/100.
